subject: frontend-engineering
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Coverage, Philosophy of the skill, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and current web theming best practices (three-tier tokens, CSS custom properties, DTCG token format, pre-paint application, runtime switching).

cases.scenario: A codebase hard-codes hex values and a flat set of variables like --gray-100, --gray-900, --blue used directly in components. The team wants to add a dark theme.
cases.context: Components currently reference appearance directly; there is no semantic layer.
cases.question: How should the agent restructure the tokens to make a dark theme possible without per-component edits?
expected_flags: Introduce a three-tier structure: reference tokens (raw values), system/semantic tokens (intent-named), component tokens
Migrate components to consume only semantic tokens (color.background.surface, color.text.primary), never raw values
Define each theme as a mapping from reference values into the system layer, scoped to :root and [data-theme="dark"]
After migration, the dark theme is a new set of system-token values with no component changes
expected_fix_hints: Replace direct --gray-100 usage in components with semantic tokens
Keep reference tokens out of component code; map them in the system layer per theme
absent_signals: Do not just add a second flat set of --gray-*-dark variables and toggle them in components
Do not let components keep referencing reference/raw values

cases.scenario: An SSR app reads the user's saved theme from localStorage in a useEffect after mount, so users briefly see the light theme before it flips to dark on every load.
cases.context: The app server-renders and the team wants no flash of the wrong theme.
cases.question: How should the agent eliminate the theme flash?
expected_flags: Apply the theme (class or data attribute on the document root) before first paint, not in a post-mount effect
Use a small inline script in the document head that runs before the stylesheet loads to set the theme attribute
For SSR, serialize the chosen theme into the initial HTML (e.g. via a cookie) so server output matches user preference
Persist the choice in localStorage or a cookie (cookie if SSR needs it server-side)
expected_fix_hints: Move theme application from useEffect to a pre-paint inline head script
Store the preference in a cookie so the server can render the right theme
absent_signals: Do not apply the theme only after React mounts
Do not rely on a CSS transition to 'hide' the flash

cases.scenario: A product has light and dark themes and now needs a high-contrast theme. A developer proposes adding conditional logic in several components to special-case high-contrast.
cases.context: The token contract already has a semantic layer; components consume semantic tokens.
cases.question: How should the agent add the third theme?
expected_flags: Add the third theme by providing a new set of system-token values scoped to a new selector ([data-theme="high-contrast"])
No component files should be modified to support the new theme
Verify the new theme covers every semantic token the existing themes define (theme parity)
Reject per-component conditional logic as a violation of the indirection contract
expected_fix_hints: Author a high-contrast value map over the existing semantic tokens
Check for missing tokens so none fall back to invalid/unintended values
absent_signals: Do not add per-component high-contrast branches
Do not introduce raw values in components for the new theme

cases.scenario: A team wants to rename color.background.surface to color.surface.default and assumes a find-and-replace plus a CSS fallback value will keep things working.
cases.context: Many components consume the token by exact name; the renamed token will be a different custom property.
cases.question: How should the agent handle the rename safely?
expected_flags: Renaming or removing a system token is a breaking change requiring a deprecation cycle, not a silent swap
A missing token resolves to the CSS variable fallback (or invalid) at runtime — rarely what's wanted in production
Make the removal/rename fail loudly at build or lint time across every consumer, not silently at runtime
Adding a new token is safe; renaming/removing is the breaking case to manage
expected_fix_hints: Introduce the new token, migrate consumers, then deprecate and remove the old token
Add a build/lint check that errors on consumption of a removed token
absent_signals: Do not rely on a CSS fallback value to mask the rename
Do not assume find-and-replace covers imperative/runtime token reads

cases.scenario: After switching themes at runtime, the CSS-styled UI updates instantly but a charting library and a canvas keep rendering with the old theme colors.
cases.context: The chart and canvas read colors imperatively in JS, not via CSS custom properties.
cases.question: How should the agent make the imperative consumers respect the theme switch?
expected_flags: Runtime switching needs a propagation step: notify components that read theme imperatively (chart libraries, canvases)
Re-read the resolved token values (e.g. getComputedStyle of the custom properties) and re-render the imperative consumers on theme change
CSS-bound UI updates automatically via cascading custom properties; imperative consumers do not
Keep a single source of truth for token values so JS reads the same values CSS does
expected_fix_hints: Subscribe imperative components to a theme-change event and re-render
Read token values from the CSS custom properties rather than hard-coding them in JS
absent_signals: Do not hard-code separate color constants in the chart/canvas code
Do not assume a CSS-only switch updates JS-driven renderers

cases.scenario: A PM asks the theme-system owner to pick the exact shade of the new brand purple and to wire up prefers-color-scheme so the app auto-follows the OS dark mode.
cases.context: The team conflates 'theming' with all color and dark-mode work.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: Choosing the exact purple / designing the palette is out of scope — route to color-system-design
prefers-color-scheme detection and OS-following behavior is out of scope — route to dark-mode-implementation
Offer the in-scope part: which semantic token the purple maps to and how the OS-driven theme plugs into the switching contract
Correctly redirects rather than answering out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Hand value selection to color-system-design and OS detection to dark-mode-implementation
Define the semantic token and the theme-switch hook the detected preference will drive
absent_signals: Do not pick the brand color value
Do not implement prefers-color-scheme detection as theme-system work
